scope_note: Breadth catalog only. IDENTIFIED_ONLY entries have no AEGIS generator or reported detector performance; only the existing three AttackFamily values are deeply simulated.

scenarios.name: Synthetic identity trust build and bust-out
scenarios.genai_abuse_mechanism: Synthetic imagery, forged identity documents, biometric spoofing, and large-scale assembly of blended identity profiles make onboarding abuse cheaper.
scenarios.plausibility_evidence_note: Mastercard describes GenAI-assisted onboarding artifacts, dormancy, credit building, and eventual bust-out. AEGIS implements only a PaySim-derived behavioral analogue.

evidence_sources.title: Mastercard: Securing the digital ecosystem with AI

scenarios.name: Mule network micro-structuring and layering
scenarios.genai_abuse_mechanism: No criminal GenAI mechanism is required or claimed by the cited evidence. In AEGIS, GenAI may only propose bounded simulator parameters; it does not create mule rows.
scenarios.plausibility_evidence_note: Mastercard explicitly documents micro-structuring and mule-account networks on RTP rails. The GenAI recruitment link is a bounded hypothesis, not a measured result.

scenarios.name: Feedback-guided detector evasion
scenarios.genai_abuse_mechanism: A reasoning model can prioritize bounded parameter variants from observed outcomes; the deterministic simulator, never GenAI, produces transaction rows.
observable_signals: risk scores below a fixed action threshold
scenarios.plausibility_evidence_note: This is an AEGIS synthetic-only adversarial benchmark. It demonstrates a bounded research loop and does not claim real-world probing access or evasion capability.

scenarios.name: Deepfake impersonation leading to authorized push payment fraud
scenarios.genai_abuse_mechanism: Voice cloning and deepfake video impersonate a trusted person or authority and induce the victim to authorize an otherwise valid payment.
scenarios.plausibility_evidence_note: Mastercard documents AI-simulated voices and deepfake endorsements as APP-fraud enablers. PaySim lacks victim-contact and authorization-intent evidence.

scenarios.name: GenAI-scaled phishing followed by account takeover
scenarios.genai_abuse_mechanism: GenAI produces convincing, targeted phishing messages and sites at scale; stolen credentials are then used to control a legitimate account.
scenarios.plausibility_evidence_note: Mastercard links GenAI-scaled phishing to account takeover and unauthorized money movement. A transaction-only simulator cannot represent the compromise stage.

scenarios.name: GenAI-built scam merchant and goods-not-delivered purchase fraud
scenarios.genai_abuse_mechanism: Professional-looking storefronts, ads, testimonials, and deepfake endorsements are generated quickly to make a fake merchant appear legitimate.
scenarios.plausibility_evidence_note: Mastercard describes AI-generated scam storefronts that take card payments, fail to deliver goods, and may harvest credentials. PaySim has no merchant lifecycle.

scenarios.name: Merchant account takeover and settlement redirection
scenarios.genai_abuse_mechanism: GenAI-enhanced phishing can acquire merchant credentials; the attacker then changes routing details or intercepts customer payments.
observable_signals: inherited merchant volume followed by anomalies
scenarios.plausibility_evidence_note: Mastercard documents takeover of reputable merchant accounts followed by routing changes and payment interception. Settlement state is absent from PaySim.

scenarios.name: Payment-credential harvesting followed by card-not-present fraud
scenarios.genai_abuse_mechanism: GenAI improves phishing copy and fake-site quality; harvested card details are used for later unauthorized e-commerce purchases.
scenarios.plausibility_evidence_note: Mastercard describes GenAI phishing, checkout-page skimming, credential harvesting, and subsequent fraudulent card purchases. PaySim is not a card-authorization corpus.

scenarios.name: BIN enumeration and card testing
scenarios.genai_abuse_mechanism: The evidenced enabler is automation rather than GenAI. GenAI may support upstream fake-merchant content, but this taxonomy does not claim it generates valid cards.
observable_signals: many cards per merchant or device
scenarios.plausibility_evidence_note: Mastercard explicitly documents automated BIN enumeration and bot-driven card testing. The limited GenAI role is stated to avoid overstating the evidence.

scenarios.plausibility_evidence_note: Mastercard separately identifies BNPL abuse as a growing payment risk and GenAI-made identity artifacts as an onboarding risk; AEGIS does not claim a measured causal link.
